# Python 3.10.22, 3.11.17, 3.12.15, 3.13.16 and 3.14.8 are now available!
A full sweep of Python releases is here: **Python 3.10.22, 3.11.17, 3.12.15, 3.13.16 and 3.14.8 are now available!** One last lap around the Sun for Python 3.10, and security updates across all five series.
...
**Python 3.10.22 is the final release of Python 3.10.** After five years, the series has reached end of life and will receive no further security updates.
...
Python 3.11 remains in security-fix-only mode until October 2027, as described in PEP 664.
Security releases are made as needed, with no fixed cadence.
...
These two releases contain security fixes rather than new features.
...
Python 3.14.8 is a maintenance release, and both 3.13.16 and 3.14.8 include binary installers.
...
## Security content in all five releases
- gh-158446: Fix crashes or incorrect output when formatting float or complex values with precision close to INT_MAX.
- CVE-2026-19553 — gh-156793: `ssl.SSLContext.wrap_bio()` now validates its `server_side`, `server_hostname`, and `session` arguments.
`asyncio` also validates TLS `server_hostname` arguments.
On Python 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12, missing hostnames with `check_hostname` enabled emit `DeprecationWarning` for compatibility; they raise `ValueError` on Python 3.13 and later.
- gh-157953: Update bundled libexpat to version 2.8.5.
- CVE-2026-15310 — gh-156002: Bound `zipfile` decompression per read for bzip2 and LZMA members, and for Zstandard members on Python 3.14, preventing unbounded allocations from small compressed members.
Third-party decompressors supplied by monkey-patching `_get_decompressor()` that lack `needs_input` and two-argument `decompress()` remain vulnerable.
- CVE-2026-19672 — gh-155999: Prevent tarfile extraction filters from creating directories outside the destination for paths that leave it and then return.
- CVE-2026-19445 — gh-156293: Fix an ssl crash when an SNI callback switches contexts and the original callback context is no longer referenced.
- CVE-2026-17084 — gh-155292: Restrict stringprep and the IDNA codec to Unicode codepoint attributes defined by RFC 3454.
- CVE-2026-15806 — gh-155694: Scope urllib.request HTTPPasswordMgr credentials by URL scheme to prevent HTTPS credentials from being used for matching HTTP URLs.
...
## Additional security content by version
### Python 3.10.22, 3.11.17, 3.12.15 and 3.13.16
- CVE-2026-82049 — gh-157190: Fix a tarfile extraction-filter vulnerability involving hard links to symbolic links that could expose files outside the destination and change their permissions or modification times.
Python 3.14 and later were already protected because `os.link()` follows symbolic links since Python 3.14.0b1 (gh-81793).
- CVE-2026-87910 — gh-157265: Apply tarfile extraction filters when a link falls back to extracting an archive member, skipping members rejected by the filter.
### Python 3.13.16 and 3.14.8
- gh-158010: Update bundled OpenSSL to 3.5.9.
In Python 3.13.16 this applies to Windows, macOS and Android, moving from OpenSSL 3.0.21 to the 3.5 LTS series.
In Python 3.14.8 it applies to Windows, macOS, Android and iOS.
...
### Python 3.10.22
- gh-149018: Improve protection against XML hash-flooding attacks in `xml.parsers.expat` and `xml.etree.ElementTree` when compiled with libexpat 2.8.0 or later.

## Major new features of the 3.15 series, compared to 3.14
Some of the major new features and changes in Python 3.15 are:
### Interpreter improvements
- PEP 810: Explicit lazy imports for faster startup times
- PEP 814: Add `frozendict` built-in type
- PEP 661: Add `sentinel` built-in type
- PEP 798: Unpacking in comprehensions
- PEP 686: Python now uses UTF-8 as the default encoding
- PEP 829: Package startup configuration files
- The experimental JIT compiler has been significantly upgraded, with 7-8% geometric mean performance improvement on x86-64 Linux over the standard interpreter, and 11-12% speedup on AArch64 macOS over the tail-calling interpreter
### Significant improvements in the standard library
- PEP 799: Tachyon: High frequency statistical sampling profiler
- PEP 799: A dedicated profiling package for organizing Python profiling tools
### New typing features
- PEP 728: `TypedDict` with typed extra items
- PEP 747: Annotating type forms with `TypeForm`
- PEP 800: Disjoint bases in the type system
### C API improvements
- PEP 803, 820, 793: Stable ABI for free-threaded builds and related C API
- PEP 782: A new `PyBytesWriter` C API to create a Python bytes object
- PEP 788: Protection against finalization in the C API
### Build changes
- PEP 831: Frame pointers are enabled by default for improved system-level observability
### Release changes
- The official Windows 64-bit binaries now use the tail-calling interpreter
- The official macOS binaries now install free-threading support by default
...

# Thoughts on Python 3.15.0 RC3
I’ve been testing the newly released Python 3.15.0 RC3, and I’d like to share some brief thoughts.
This is the final planned release candidate for Python 3.15, as mentioned on the official release page:
> “This release, 3.15.0 rc3, is the final planned release candidate.”
...
### Python Release Python 3.15.0rc3
We got some last-minute lazy-import release blockers, and it makes sense to include them in 3.15.0 final.
...
One of the features I’m most interested in is the improved free-threading support.
I tried a simple multi-threaded script with the `--disable-gil` build and observed real parallel execution on multi-core CPUs.
...
It’s exciting to see the GIL-free build getting more stable with each release candidate.
I also noticed the new built-in `frozendict` type from PEP 814.
Immutable dictionaries will be really helpful for caching and constant configuration objects.

# Free-Threaded Python Post-Era (Python Language Summit 2026)
## Behavior-Oriented Concurrency (BOC)
Behavior-Oriented Concurrency (BOC) is the model the trio is proposing for a high-level concurrency interface for Python.
Programs written with the BOC model are task-based.
Tasks are lightweight, can run on any core, and cannot deadlock.
...
The bocpy package provides three features:
- “Cowns”, or locks with ownership
- Behaviors (the tasks spawned with `@when` decorators)
- Scheduler (implemented with subinterpreters, with planned support for free-threading)

# Rust for CPython (Python Language Summit 2026)
## Why Rust?
“We’ve been making some big technical bets”, he said, referencing the new parser, the JIT, and free-threading.
...
The proposal would be to ask Python distributors to attempt using the optional Rust support in Python 3.16 (October 2027) and report platform-specific issues upstream in time to be resolved around the Python 3.17 timeline (October 2028).
...
## The proposed first Rust module: zlib
Under this timeline, the first Rust code to ship in Python would be in Python 3.16, where it would be completely optional, with the existing C code kept as a fallback.
The earliest that Rust would become required to build CPython is Python 3.18 in 2029, at least three years away.
The timeline includes a build system and CI, Rust API proof-of-concept happening
in the Summer 2026, a PEP defining success criteria in late 2026,
an optional Rust backend for the zlib module and private Rust API in Python 3.16 (October 2027),
resolving platform issues and Rust in more places (io, json, xml, memoryview, parser)
for Python 3.17 (October 2028).
...
The Rust for CPython team has selected the zlib module as the first module to be given an optional Rust implementation because they “wanted to achieve a significant improvement” with a “small scope”.

# Pre-PEP: UTF-8 String Representation
## Reference implementation
#### Change Unicode's internal representation to UTF-8 (#134)
This pull request introduces significant changes to the internal representation …and C API for Unicode objects in Python, focusing on optimizing storage, clarifying documentation, and improving error handling.
The main update is that Unicode objects now primarily store UTF-8 directly and generate the fixed-width representation (FSR) on demand, which can fail with an exception.
...
**Unicode object internal representation and storage:** * Unicode objects now store UTF-8 directly after the object header, with ASCII strings sharing this storage; the fixed-width representation (FSR) is generated on demand and retained until object destruction.
...
## Specification
- Ordinary non-ASCII strings retain a UTF-8 representation.
The PEP 393 fixed-width representation (FSR) is created and retained only when needed.
- Lone surrogates are preserved internally using `surrogatepass`, without changing Python-level semantics such as string length and indexing.
- Strings under construction with `PyUnicode_New()` continue to use a writable FSR.
- Many paths, including string operations, `UnicodeWriter`, codecs, and JSON, have been changed to process UTF-8 directly or read characters sequentially.
- `PyUnicode_KIND()` returns the width of the fixed-width representation.
`PyUnicode_DATA()` and the various `*_DATA()` functions create the FSR lazily, so they may return `NULL` if memory is exhausted.
- `PyUnicode_READ_CHAR()` and `PyUnicode_ReadChar()` normally create an FSR cache and read from it.
...
- Writes are limited to construction buffers created by `PyUnicode_New()`.
Calling `PyUnicode_WriteChar()`, `PyUnicode_Fill()`, or `PyUnicode_CopyCharacters()` on a string whose primary representation is UTF-8 calls `abort()`.
A UTF-8 representation is generated for construction-buffer strings when they are read.
- `PyUnicode_New()` and the write APIs will be deprecated.
When these APIs are removed in the future, we plan to maintain O(1) random access using a more efficient position table, similar to PyPy’s.

content.text: As of October 9, 2026, Python 3.15.0 is the latest release; it adds explicit lazy imports, built-in `frozendict` and `sentinel` types, and unpacking in comprehensions. It also makes UTF-8 the default encoding and substantially upgrades the experimental JIT. [Python Insider](https://blog.python.org/2026/10/python-3150-rc3/)
